title: Peel officers cleared in man's death
subtitle: The province's Special Investigations Unit has found that Peel police officers were not criminally responsible in last year's death of a Brampton man, who died less than 12 hours after being Tasered while in police custody.
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has found that Peel police officers were not criminally responsible in last year's death of a Brampton man, who died less than 12 hours after being Tasered while in police custody.
The investigation stemmed from an incident on Sept. 16, 2008, involving 42-year-old Sean Reilly, who was earlier arrested for assault with a weapon and drug possession.
While in custody at the 12 Division police station in Mississauga, Reilly was reportedly seen on a cell monitor banging his head against the bars.

Police entered the cell to take Reilly to a hospital but he allegedly ran at one of the officers and struggled while others tried to hold him down. One officer then deployed a Taser and Reilly stopped breathing shortly after.
Less than 12 hours later, he was pronounced dead at Trillium Health Centre in Mississauga.

As with any death involving a police officer, an investigation was immediately started by the SIU. Today, director Ian Scott concluded that there are "no reasonable grounds" to believe the police officers involved were criminally responsible for Reilly's death.

"Given the circumstances leading to the death of Mr. Reilly, I am of the view that the four subject officers' conduct fell within the limits prescribed by the criminal law," Mr. Scott said in a written statement.
"Accordingly, I cannot attach criminal liability to their acts and omissions with respect to this incident."
The cause of Reilly's death will be determined by a mandatory inquest, which has not yet been scheduled, said SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon.
